sections.herbal_remedies:
About Hyperthyroidism 
 Hyperthyroidism is a condition of the thyroid that occurs when it makes too much T4, T3, or both. The problem leads to several other problems as well, such as rapid heart rate, elevated blood pressure, and hand tremors. Early diagnosis of the thyroid disorder can help to get an early treatment and thereby helps in preventing several complications.
sections.what_are_the_causes_of_hyperthyroidism:
The most common cause of this thyroid disorder is grave’s disease. It is actually an autoimmune disorder that causes the antibodies to release the hormone in excess. The disorder is more common in women than men. Other common causes of this disorder are listed below:- 

 Excess production of iodine. 
 Inflammation of the thyroid (thyroiditis). 
 Tumors of the ovaries or testes. 
 Benign tumors of the thyroid or pituitary gland.
sections.the_common_symptoms_of_this_thyroid_diso:
Increased appetite. 
 Weakness and nervousness. 
 Nausea and vomiting. 
 Irregular heartbeat. 
 Elevated blood pressure. 
 Restlessness and inability to concentrate. 
 Hair loss. 
 Itching. 
 Weight loss. 

 How can Hyperthyroidism be Diagnosed? 
 There are some tests that can help to diagnose the disorder. Your doctor may diagnose the disease by simply knowing your symptoms. For more confirmation he can ask for T4, T3 and TSH level test. For more complicated condition, ultrasound, and thyroid scan test are there.
sections.what_are_the_risk_factors_for_hyperthyro: The disorder is believed to run in families. It is more common in women as compared to men. Several diseases are there which can worsen the condition of this disorder.
sections.what_are_the_complications_of_hyperthyro:
The disorder is known to have several complications. So a disorder must be treated well in order to stay away from the complications as well. Some of the well-known complications are listed below:- 

 Heart diseases are the major and serious complication of this disorder. 
 Untreated disorder can lead to weak and fragile bones. 
 The disorder may cause problem related to eyes. It can weaken the eyesight. 
 This disorder may affect the skin that can cause redness and swelling in the skin. 
 The disorder may also pose a person at risk of Thyrotoxic crisis. In this condition, symptoms lead to fever and rapid pulse.

 Ayurveda, an oldest health care system, offers a natural treatment for hyperthyroidism. It helps to balance the secretion of the thyroid gland with the help of natural herbs, controlled diet and healthy lifestyle. This disorder cures by balancing the aggravated doshas.

The disorder is believed to occur due to aggravation of vata and pitta dosha. Imbalanced vata and pitta go into minute channels of the body and in turn causes the symptoms of hyperthyroidism. The aggravated doshas lead to the overstimulation of gastric fire and in turn causes increased appetite. 
 As pitta is very hot, there will be excessive sweating and intolerance towards heat.

The main aim of the treatment by Ayurveda for the same disorder involves the clearance of the blocked channels. This will balance the body energies and in turn restore the proper circulation and production of thyroxin hormone by thyroid gland.
